clue.text: A strong company needs backing for a musical? Yes!

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
a firm is a business company

indicators.note: backing means the musical's name is read from back to front

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: A theatre producer asks whether a solid company will back a stage show, and the answer is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong company' reads as one phrase, but 'strong' is the musical F (forte) and 'company' a separate word. 'Backing' looks like financial support; here it turns the musical's name round.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative is a reply of agreement, the formal equivalent of saying yes.

clue.text: Somewhat heated — losing head — set to explode?

indicators.note: losing head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: warm means somewhat heated, not quite hot

explanation.surface: Something getting warm and losing its top suggests a device on the point of going off.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm a bomb or fuse is to make it ready to detonate.

clue.text: Shrub or trees, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for trees is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: A gardener's question: is this a bush or some trees?
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech FIRS and FURZE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze, also called gorse, is a spiny yellow-flowered evergreen bush.

clue.text: Celebrate about author's announcement

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: announcement signals the author's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: James Joyce is the Irish author of Ulysses

explanation.surface: People celebrate news concerning a writer's latest announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy, as at a celebration.

clue.text: Feeling numb again — sale going wrong?

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters of these two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper feels numb once more as a sale fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for absence of pain sensation, being numbed.

clue.text: Final stage of motorway put up in the past

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: The last section of a motorway was built some time back.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; read as M and I it reverses to IM.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final, adult phase of an insect's metamorphosis.

clue.text: Precise type of railway service

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an adjective, explicit and exact
second meaning: a fast train with few stops

explanation.definitionFit: Express means definite and explicit, and is also the name of a fast, limited-stop train.

clue.text: Glossy black spout

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... black, the colour of the polished stone
second meaning: a stream spurting from a nozzle

explanation.definitionFit: Jet names both a deep shiny black mineral and a forceful stream of liquid.

clue.text: Submarine menace with explosive — search below

indicators.note: below in a down clue places the search word under the explosive

parts.note: jelly is slang for gelignite, an explosive
to fish is to search or grope for something

explanation.surface: An underwater threat combining explosives with something hunting beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' looks like a vessel, but here it means simply undersea.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging sea creature is a danger lurking under the water to swimmers.

clue.text: Expert at stuffing tried it with Xmas cooking

indicators.note: cooking means these letters are worked up into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at stuffing a Christmas turkey tried it while preparing the festive meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The stuffing looks culinary, matching 'Xmas cooking'; it is the stuffing of dead animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxidermist preserves animal skins by filling and mounting them for display.

clue.text: Pot plant — the alternative judge's put in

indicators.note: put in means J is put in place of a letter of the alternative spelling

parts.note: marihuana is the alternative spelling of the word for cannabis
J is the abbreviation for judge; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A judge rules on a cannabis plant offered as an alternative remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug's name has two spellings, with H or J; putting J (judge) in place of the H in the alternative gives the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis, smoked as the drug called pot, comes from this hemp plant.

clue.text: One in bed reciting numbers of sheep

indicators.note: reciting means the word is spoken aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: flocks are groups of sheep

explanation.surface: Someone lying in bed counts sheep to get to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flowerbed, not one for sleeping in.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a garden perennial grown in flower borders.

clue.text: Looking to compete with political group

parts.note: to vie is to compete
a wing is a faction of a political party

explanation.surface: A politician is looking to compete with a party faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewing means watching or inspecting, the act of looking at something.

clue.text: Throwing in a double act unsuitable for radio

definitions.text: Throwing in a double act unsuitable for radio

parts.words: Throwing in a double act unsuitable for radio
parts.note: the throwing is of the voice, done by a performer with a dummy as partner; on radio no one can see the lips stay still

explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing' suggests a contest; the voice is what is thrown, and the double act is performer plus dummy.
explanation.definitionFit: This art of making one's voice seem to come from a puppet only impresses when the audience can watch.

clue.text: A person I'd announced as a literary giant

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a person is one, followed by I'd

explanation.surface: Someone announces a famous writer as a giant of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant is not a great author but a Cyclops such as Polyphemus in Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature's Cyclops has a single eye in the middle of his forehead.

clue.text: Very well-conceived sort of prize has a twist in the tail

indicators.text: has a twist in the tail
indicators.note: a twist in the tail means only the last two letters are swapped round

parts.note: the Nobel Prize is awarded annually for science, literature and peace

explanation.surface: A prize idea is clever, with a surprise ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-conceived' looks like praise for a plan; it means of good birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means of aristocratic birth, so conceived of high-ranking parents.

clue.text: Attack half of what's included in public transport cut

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: included in means the half word is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly

indicators.note: half of means the first two of the word's four letters

parts.note: the word what, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A slashed public-transport service is criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a description of the transport, a service reduced; it is a separate word for hack.
explanation.definitionFit: To bushwhack is to ambush, launching a surprise assault from cover.

clue.text: Giving more in a ball-game, one about to be over

parts.note: squash is a racket game played with a small ball
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to be over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: re means about

explanation.surface: A squash player gives more in a match, one about to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving' is yielding under pressure, not generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something squashier yields more readily when pressed, being softer.

clue.text: Odd cut in play after revision

indicators.note: after revision means the letters have been reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange cut made to a play once rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Untypical means unusual or not representative, so strange.

clue.text: Turning out part of army, head of state has little time

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a sultan rules some Muslim states
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A ruler turns out a section of the army with little time to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Resultant describes what follows as a consequence, how things turn out.

clue.text: Leaves to celebrate a triumph

parts.note: a victor was crowned with a wreath of bay leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, someone departing; it is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay foliage wreaths honoured winners in ancient Greece, hence honours won.

clue.text: A dim recollection about start of Handel's "Messiah"

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round that first letter
recollection, read as re-collection, means the letters are gathered again in a new order
start of means the first letter of Handel's

explanation.surface: A hazy memory of how Handel's oratorio begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messiah' looks like the oratorio's title; it is the definition, and Handel only gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam, the Mahdi is the prophesied redeemer expected at the end of time.

clue.text: Reviewed in Times as an artist

indicators.note: reviewed means the letters are looked over again and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter is reviewed in The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter famous for Fauvism and paper cut-outs.

clue.text: Case in which PM once put clothes

parts.note: Andrew Bonar Law was British Prime Minister in 1922-23
a suit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: A legal case in which a former prime minister got dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal action brought in court, a case.

clue.text: Banned, thanks to catcall?

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a boo is a jeering shout of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone is barred because of jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboo means prohibited by custom or rule.

clue.text: A minor beating? Exploit a bit of advice, making comeback

indicators.note: making comeback means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to tap a resource is to exploit it
a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A sports team suffers a minor defeat but uses advice to stage a recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating' suggests defeat; it is a light rhythmic beat, as of a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit-a-pat is a quick light tapping, like a fluttering heartbeat.

clue.text: Edge in very quietly, and smarten up

indicators.note: in places the edge inside the musical abbreviation

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, the musical direction for very quietly
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Someone sidles in silently and tidies themselves up.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom oneself fussily, tidying hair and clothes.

clue.text: Friend has no right to make one ' shudder

indicators.note: has no means the abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends

explanation.surface: A friend without any right is enough to make someone shudder.
explanation.definitionFit: To quake is to tremble or shake, as with fear.

clue.text: Cocktail with a kick — sick female comes staggering in

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the word for kick

parts.note: a buzz is a thrill or kick

indicators.note: staggering suggests unsteady movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A potent drink leaves a woman feeling ill and staggering home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a kick' seems to describe the drink's strength; the kick is a buzz, a thrill, which wraps the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck's fizz is a mixed drink of champagne and orange juice.

clue.text: The final thing duplicated in puzzle, in more ways than one

definitions.text: The final thing duplicated in puzzle, in more ways than one

parts.words: The final thing duplicated in puzzle, in more ways than one
parts.note: the last letter of the alphabet appears twice in the word puzzle, and also twice in this grid

explanation.walkthrough: The word puzzle contains a doubled letter, and that last letter also appears twice in this very crossword, at 25 and 26.
explanation.definitionFit: Zed is the British name for Z, the alphabet's last letter.

clue.text: Hairy beast has girl in a spin

indicators.note: in a spin means the name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shaggy animal sends a young woman into a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A yak is a long-haired ox of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Clothing accessory ought to drape differently

parts.note: should means ought

indicators.note: differently means the letters of drape are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Advice that a garment ought to hang another way.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder pad is padding sewn into a jacket or dress to shape the shoulders.
